---
title: "Raster Gap Filler"
date: 2026-09-20
categories: [tool, geostatistics]
description: "Upload a multi-band raster and fill the gaps in one band using a second, correlated band as a covariate — cokriging instead of single-variable kriging. Runs entirely in your browser, powered by R."
page-layout: full
---

Upload a raster with two or more bands — a satellite band with cloud
gaps, a field survey rasterized with mostly-empty cells, anything with
real holes in it — pick the band to fill (the *target*) and, if you
have one, a second band that's correlated with it (the *covariate*,
elevation or another spectral band are common choices). The covariate
can have gaps of its own: pixels missing in both bands stay empty.
This tool fits a variogram model between the two, then predicts the
target's missing values from wherever the covariate is available —
cokriging, not just averaging nearby pixels. Skip the covariate and it
falls back to ordinary kriging on the target band's own known pixels.

::: {.callout-tip}
**Private by design.** Your file is processed entirely in your browser
(R via WebAssembly) — it's never uploaded to any server, including
ours. Nothing to configure, nothing to trust: the code never gets the
chance to see your data.
:::

```{.webgeods-r #raster-gap-filler-inspect-r .tool-cell}
#| package: terra, jsonlite
library(terra)

path <- NULL
for (candidate in c("/uploaded.tif")) {
  ok <- tryCatch({ rast(candidate); TRUE }, error = function(e) FALSE)
  if (ok) { path <- candidate; break }
}

summary_out <- NULL
footprint <- list(type = jsonlite::unbox("FeatureCollection"), features = list())
bands_out <- list()

if (!is.null(path)) {
  r <- rast(path)

  # Per-band valid/NA counts -- the whole reason this needs its own
  # pass before the reader picks anything: a band with a lot of NA is
  # a plausible target, a band with none is a plausible covariate, and
  # neither is obvious from band count/names alone.
  band_stats <- lapply(seq_len(nlyr(r)), function(i) {
    band <- r[[i]]
    n_total <- ncell(band)
    n_na <- as.numeric(global(is.na(band), "sum")[1, 1])
    list(
      band = jsonlite::unbox(i),
      name = jsonlite::unbox(names(r)[i]),
      naCount = jsonlite::unbox(n_na),
      naFraction = jsonlite::unbox(round(n_na / n_total, 4))
    )
  })

  # Suggested target: the band with the most NA (ties broken by lower
  # index) -- a default, not a lock, the reader can always pick a
  # different pair.
  na_fractions <- sapply(band_stats, function(b) b$naFraction)
  suggested_target <- if (any(na_fractions > 0)) which.max(na_fractions) else 1

  # as.vector(ext(r)) keeps its own names (xmin/xmax/ymin/ymax) --
  # jsonlite serializes a NAMED numeric as a JSON object ({"xmin":
  # 12.4}), not a plain number, so each coordinate needs an explicit
  # as.numeric() (unname() alone isn't enough once it's inside a
  # list()) before it can sit inside a GeoJSON coordinate pair.
  bnds <- as.vector(ext(r))
  xmin <- as.numeric(bnds["xmin"]); xmax <- as.numeric(bnds["xmax"])
  ymin <- as.numeric(bnds["ymin"]); ymax <- as.numeric(bnds["ymax"])
  footprint <- list(
    type = jsonlite::unbox("FeatureCollection"),
    features = list(list(
      type = jsonlite::unbox("Feature"),
      properties = list(name = jsonlite::unbox("raster footprint")),
      geometry = list(
        type = jsonlite::unbox("Polygon"),
        coordinates = list(list(
          list(xmin, ymin), list(xmax, ymin),
          list(xmax, ymax), list(xmin, ymax),
          list(xmin, ymin)
        ))
      )
    ))
  )

  # Same reprojection this cell's own compute/export siblings already
  # need (a bare SpatExtent can't go through project() directly; see
  # their own comment for why) -- the live target/covariate preview
  # below needs it too, to place the raster correctly for a file whose
  # native CRS isn't already WGS84.
  to_minx_miny_maxx_maxy <- function(spat_extent) {
    b <- as.vector(spat_extent)
    c(as.numeric(b["xmin"]), as.numeric(b["ymin"]), as.numeric(b["xmax"]), as.numeric(b["ymax"]))
  }
  wgs84_bounds <- tryCatch({
    poly_wgs84 <- project(as.polygons(ext(r), crs = crs(r)), "EPSG:4326")
    to_minx_miny_maxx_maxy(ext(poly_wgs84))
  }, error = function(e) to_minx_miny_maxx_maxy(ext(r)))

  # Every band's own raw values, base64-encoded the same way the
  # compute cell encodes its filled result -- lets the map preview the
  # target/covariate bands the reader currently has picked WITHOUT a
  # round trip through R each time they change a dropdown (cokriging
  # itself only runs once Fill is actually pressed).
  bands_out <- lapply(seq_len(nlyr(r)), function(i) {
    vals <- as.numeric(values(r[[i]]))
    valid <- vals[!is.na(vals)]
    con <- rawConnection(raw(0), "wb")
    writeBin(vals, con, size = 4, endian = "little")
    raw_bytes <- rawConnectionValue(con)
    close(con)
    list(
      band = jsonlite::unbox(i),
      data = jsonlite::unbox(jsonlite::base64_enc(raw_bytes)),
      min = if (length(valid) > 0) jsonlite::unbox(min(valid)) else NULL,
      max = if (length(valid) > 0) jsonlite::unbox(max(valid)) else NULL
    )
  })

  summary_out <- list(
    width = jsonlite::unbox(ncol(r)),
    height = jsonlite::unbox(nrow(r)),
    bandCount = jsonlite::unbox(nlyr(r)),
    crs = jsonlite::unbox(crs(r, describe = TRUE)$name),
    bandStats = band_stats,
    suggestedTarget = jsonlite::unbox(suggested_target),
    wgs84Bounds = round(wgs84_bounds, 6)
  )
}

list(summary = summary_out, footprint = footprint, bands = bands_out)
```

The code itself isn't shown here — it's a fixed, non-editable
computation using `gstat`'s cokriging (linear model of
coregionalization) underneath. Want to see the same pipeline built up
one step at a time, why a covariate band helps, and why this runs on
R, not Python? Read
[Filling Raster Gaps with Cokriging](/posts/cokriging-raster-gap-filling.html).

```{.webgeods-r #raster-gap-filler-compute-r .tool-cell}
#| inject: [targetBand, covariateBand, variogramModel, nmax]
#| package: sf, sp, gstat, terra, jsonlite
library(sf)
library(sp)
library(gstat)
library(terra)

target_i <- as.integer(targetBand)
covariate_i <- if (identical(covariateBand, "None")) NA_integer_ else as.integer(covariateBand)

if (!is.na(covariate_i) && covariate_i == target_i) {
  stop("Target and covariate must be different bands — pick two distinct bands, or set the covariate to \"None\".")
}

r <- rast("/uploaded.tif")

# The terra -> sp bridge: gstat's own variogram()/krige()/fit.lmc()
# take sp point objects (coordinates(df) <- ~x+y), not a terra
# SpatRaster or SpatVector -- terra doesn't provide that replacement
# function itself. crds()/values() give cell centers and per-band
# values aligned by row, in the file's OWN crs (no reprojection here,
# unlike kriging-interpolator.qmd's point-survey case: a raster's
# pixels already sit on a grid with a real resolution, not raw lon/lat
# survey coordinates that need a working CRS to make distance
# meaningful).
cell_xy <- crds(r, na.rm = FALSE)
target_vals <- as.numeric(values(r[[target_i]]))
df <- data.frame(x = cell_xy[, 1], y = cell_xy[, 2], target = target_vals)

has_covariate <- !is.na(covariate_i)
if (has_covariate) {
  df$covariate <- as.numeric(values(r[[covariate_i]]))
}

fit_method_used <- NA_integer_

if (!has_covariate) {

  # No covariate: ordinary kriging on the target band's own known
  # pixels, same shape as kriging-interpolator-compute-r's own
  # variogram()/fit.variogram()/krige() sequence, just with the raster's
  # OWN valid cells standing in for uploaded sample points.
  fit_df <- df[!is.na(df$target), ]
  pred_df <- df[is.na(df$target), ]

  if (nrow(fit_df) < 5) {
    stop(paste0("Need at least 5 valid pixels in the target band to fit a variogram — found ", nrow(fit_df), "."))
  }

  fit_pts <- fit_df
  coordinates(fit_pts) <- ~x + y

  v_emp <- variogram(target ~ 1, fit_pts)
  init_range <- max(v_emp$dist) / 3
  init_psill <- var(fit_df$target)
  v_model <- tryCatch(
    fit.variogram(v_emp, vgm(psill = init_psill, model = variogramModel, range = init_range, nugget = init_psill / 4)),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(v_model) || isTRUE(attr(v_model, "singular")) || any(v_model$psill < 0)) {
    stop(paste0("Could not fit a ", variogramModel, " variogram model to this band's known pixels."))
  }

  cv <- tryCatch(gstat.cv(gstat(id = "target", formula = target ~ 1, data = fit_pts, model = v_model), nfold = 5, verbose = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
  rmse <- if (!is.null(cv)) sqrt(mean(cv$residual^2, na.rm = TRUE)) else NA

  filled <- df$target

  if (nrow(pred_df) > 0) {
    pred_pts <- pred_df
    coordinates(pred_pts) <- ~x + y
    k <- krige(target ~ 1, fit_pts, pred_pts, model = v_model, nmax = as.numeric(nmax), debug.level = 0)
    filled[is.na(df$target)] <- as.numeric(k$var1.pred)
  }

  # Same three numbers kriging-interpolator.qmd's own stats card
  # reports, plus the fitting sample's own mean/variance -- nugget +
  # partial sill landing far from that variance is the easiest sign a
  # fit went wrong, without this tool asserting a pass/fail verdict
  # itself (a fixed threshold would flag genuinely non-stationary data
  # as "bad" just as often as an actual bad fit).
  nugget_val <- v_model$psill[1]
  partial_sill_val <- v_model$psill[2]
  range_val <- v_model$range[2]
  sample_mean <- mean(fit_df$target)
  sample_variance <- var(fit_df$target)

  v_line <- variogramLine(v_model, maxdist = max(v_emp$dist), n = 100)
  variogram_out <- list(
    target = list(
      nugget = jsonlite::unbox(round(nugget_val, 4)),
      partialSill = jsonlite::unbox(round(partial_sill_val, 4)),
      # dist rounded to 6dp, not 3 -- this raster's own coordinates are
      # degree-scale (a range around 0.01-0.05), so 3dp was coarse
      # enough to round SEVERAL of variogramLine()'s 100 points to the
      # identical x value while their y still rose smoothly between
      # them -- found live: a fitted "curve" that was actually a
      # staircase, each repeated x plotted as a vertical jump followed
      # by a flat run to the next one.
      empirical = list(dist = round(v_emp$dist, 6), gamma = round(v_emp$gamma, 5), npairs = v_emp$np),
      fitted = list(dist = round(v_line$dist, 6), gamma = round(v_line$gamma, 5))
    )
  )

} else {

  # data_fit: pixels where BOTH bands are valid -- fitting only, never
  # prediction. data_pred: pixels where the COVARIATE is valid,
  # regardless of the target -- this must include data_fit's own
  # locations too (it does automatically, since data_fit is already a
  # subset of "covariate valid"). Do NOT narrow data_pred to just the
  # target's own gaps -- gstat needs the already-known target pixels
  # present in data_pred for the cokriging system's local context, or
  # it silently breaks.
  data_fit <- df[!is.na(df$target) & !is.na(df$covariate), ]
  data_pred <- df[!is.na(df$covariate), ]

  if (nrow(data_fit) < 5) {
    stop(paste0("Need at least 5 pixels where both the target and covariate bands are valid to fit a coregionalization model — found ", nrow(data_fit), "."))
  }

  fit_pts <- data_fit
  coordinates(fit_pts) <- ~x + y

  v_emp <- variogram(target ~ 1, fit_pts)
  init_psill <- var(data_fit$target)

  # Both variables registered on the SAME point object (fit_pts, same
  # rows, same order) -- registering them on mismatched location sets
  # instead forces gstat to compute a genuine zero-distance bin between
  # the two variables' own locations, which fit.method=7 (Cressie's
  # weights, gstat's own default) divides by.
  v_cross <- variogram(gstat(gstat(NULL, id = "target", formula = target ~ 1, data = fit_pts), id = "covariate", formula = covariate ~ 1, data = fit_pts))

  # fit.lmc()'s own optimizer is local, not global -- the single
  # init_range = max(dist)/3 guess this used to pass it (a reasonable
  # rule of thumb for an ordinary single-variable fit.variogram())
  # routinely trapped the JOINT fit in a much worse local optimum here:
  # confirmed live, trying several starting ranges on the same data,
  # sum-of-squared-error against the target's own empirical points
  # ranged from 1878 (at max/3) down to 173 (at the full max distance)
  # -- a ~10x difference, with the target's fitted sill/range moving
  # enough to visibly matter on the chart, not just in the decimals.
  # Trying a small spread of starting points and keeping whichever
  # converges closest to the target's own empirical variogram is the
  # robust fix: no single fixed fraction is a good guess for every
  # raster a reader uploads, but "try several, keep the best" doesn't
  # need to guess right the first time.
  sse_against_target <- function(model_df) {
    vl <- variogramLine(model_df, dist_vector = v_emp$dist)
    sum((v_emp$gamma - vl$gamma)^2)
  }
  fit_lmc_candidate <- function(init_range) {
    lmc_model <- vgm(psill = init_psill, model = variogramModel, range = init_range, nugget = init_psill / 4)
    fresh_g <- function() gstat(gstat(NULL, id = "target", formula = target ~ 1, data = fit_pts), id = "covariate", formula = covariate ~ 1, data = fit_pts)
    gf <- tryCatch(fit.lmc(v_cross, fresh_g(), model = lmc_model, fit.method = 7, correct.diagonal = 1.01), error = function(e) NULL)
    method <- 7
    if (is.null(gf)) {
      gf <- tryCatch(fit.lmc(v_cross, fresh_g(), model = lmc_model, fit.method = 1, correct.diagonal = 1.01), error = function(e) NULL)
      method <- 1
    }
    if (is.null(gf)) return(NULL)
    list(g_fit = gf, method = method, sse = sse_against_target(gf$model[["target"]]))
  }

  candidates <- Filter(Negate(is.null), lapply(max(v_cross$dist) * c(1 / 6, 1 / 3, 2 / 3, 1), fit_lmc_candidate))
  if (length(candidates) == 0) {
    stop(paste0("Could not fit a coregionalization model between these two bands (often too few co-located pixels, or the bands aren't actually correlated)."))
  }
  best <- candidates[[which.min(sapply(candidates, function(c) c$sse))]]
  g_fit <- best$g_fit
  fit_method_used <- best$method

  # gstat.cv() on a multivariate (cokriging) gstat object names its
  # result columns "target.pred"/"target.var" (id-prefixed, since more
  # than one variable is registered) but the residual/observed/zscore
  # columns are NOT prefixed -- just "residual", found empirically
  # (cv$target.residual doesn't exist and silently produced NaN/null
  # instead of erroring, since `$` on a missing data.frame column
  # returns NULL rather than raising).
  cv <- tryCatch(gstat.cv(g_fit, nfold = 5, verbose = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
  rmse <- if (!is.null(cv)) sqrt(mean(cv$residual^2, na.rm = TRUE)) else NA

  pred_pts <- data_pred
  coordinates(pred_pts) <- ~x + y

  # Target on its own known locations (fit_pts), covariate on ALL of
  # data_pred -- then attach the already-fitted model as a SEPARATE
  # step. Passing model= directly into this gstat() call throws
  # "argument 'formula' is missing" (it reads it as a brand-new
  # variable, not the existing fit); this plain assignment after the
  # fact is the version that actually works.
  g_pred <- gstat(NULL, id = "target", formula = target ~ 1, data = fit_pts)
  g_pred <- gstat(g_pred, id = "covariate", formula = covariate ~ 1, data = pred_pts)
  g_pred$model <- g_fit$model

  k <- predict(g_pred, newdata = pred_pts, nmax = as.numeric(nmax), debug.level = 0)

  filled <- df$target
  pred_index <- which(!is.na(df$covariate))
  cokriged <- is.na(df$target[pred_index])
  filled[pred_index[cokriged]] <- as.numeric(k$target.pred[cokriged])

  # Pixels the covariate itself couldn't reach: target NA, covariate
  # also NA. Left as NA on purpose -- no fallback pass to plain kriging
  # here, see raster-gap-filler.qmd's own closing note for why (the
  # reader can rerun this tool a second time on the result, with no
  # covariate, if they want those filled too).

  # Stats card numbers: the TARGET's own component of the joint fit --
  # fit.lmc() names the three pieces of an LMC "target", "covariate"
  # and "target.covariate" (the cross term), each a normal 2-row vgm
  # model (Nug + the chosen shape), confirmed live rather than assumed
  # from the docs. Reporting target's own nugget/sill/range here keeps
  # this row meaning the same thing it means in the no-covariate
  # branch above -- the target band's own spatial structure -- even
  # though the fit that produced it also used the covariate.
  target_model <- g_fit$model[["target"]]
  covariate_model <- g_fit$model[["covariate"]]
  cross_model <- g_fit$model[["target.covariate"]]

  nugget_val <- target_model$psill[1]
  partial_sill_val <- target_model$psill[2]
  range_val <- target_model$range[2]
  sample_mean <- mean(data_fit$target)
  sample_variance <- var(data_fit$target)

  # All three curves for the side panel's charts -- v_cross already
  # holds target's, covariate's AND the cross term's empirical points
  # in one data.frame (an `id` column, not three separate calls), and
  # variogramLine() accepts each piece of g_fit$model exactly like a
  # plain fit.variogram() result. Nothing here is a new computation:
  # fit.lmc() above already produced all of it, just never read back
  # out until now. Each series carries its OWN nugget/partialSill (the
  # shared range lives once in summary$range, since fit.lmc() gives
  # every component the same range by construction) so the side panel
  # can draw a correctly-labeled reference line on all three, not just
  # the one summary already covers.
  max_dist <- max(v_cross$dist)
  # 6dp, not 3 -- same fix as the no-covariate branch above, for the
  # same reason (this raster's degree-scale coordinates need finer
  # rounding than a meter-scale one would, or variogramLine()'s 100
  # points collapse onto a handful of duplicate x values and the
  # "curve" plots as a staircase instead).
  fitted_line <- function(model_df) {
    vl <- variogramLine(model_df, maxdist = max_dist, n = 100)
    list(dist = round(vl$dist, 6), gamma = round(vl$gamma, 5))
  }
  empirical_for <- function(id_name) {
    sub <- v_cross[v_cross$id == id_name, ]
    list(dist = round(sub$dist, 6), gamma = round(sub$gamma, 5), npairs = sub$np)
  }
  variogram_out <- list(
    target = list(
      nugget = jsonlite::unbox(round(nugget_val, 4)),
      partialSill = jsonlite::unbox(round(partial_sill_val, 4)),
      empirical = empirical_for("target"), fitted = fitted_line(target_model)
    ),
    covariate = list(
      nugget = jsonlite::unbox(round(covariate_model$psill[1], 4)),
      partialSill = jsonlite::unbox(round(covariate_model$psill[2], 4)),
      empirical = empirical_for("covariate"), fitted = fitted_line(covariate_model)
    ),
    cross = list(
      nugget = jsonlite::unbox(round(cross_model$psill[1], 4)),
      partialSill = jsonlite::unbox(round(cross_model$psill[2], 4)),
      empirical = empirical_for("target.covariate"), fitted = fitted_line(cross_model)
    )
  )

}

# One definition covers both branches -- any pixel that went from NA
# to a real value, regardless of which branch (or which method inside
# it) put it there. A per-branch count here was the actual bug: the
# no-covariate branch is ordinary kriging, not "filled from
# covariate", so a field literally named that read 0 there even though
# every reachable gap really had just been filled.
n_filled <- sum(!is.na(filled)) - sum(!is.na(df$target))

n_still_na <- sum(is.na(filled))

filled_band <- rast(matrix(filled, nrow = nrow(r), ncol = ncol(r), byrow = TRUE), extent = ext(r), crs = crs(r))
names(filled_band) <- names(r)[target_i]

valid_filled <- filled[!is.na(filled)]

# terra::project() doesn't take a bare SpatExtent -- the documented,
# correct way to reproject just a bounding box is to wrap it as a
# SpatVector polygon first (as.polygons()), project THAT, then read
# its extent back. round()/as.vector() on the extent's own named
# xmin/xmax/ymin/ymax would keep those names, and jsonlite serializes
# a NAMED vector as a JSON OBJECT ({"xmin": ...}) instead of a plain
# array -- setRasterImage() (shared/map-raster.js) destructures
# `bounds` positionally ([minx, miny, maxx, maxy] = bounds), which
# throws "bounds is not iterable" on a plain object, not a graceful
# failure. Each coordinate goes through an explicit as.numeric() to
# strip its name before assembly, same fix as the footprint above.
to_minx_miny_maxx_maxy <- function(spat_extent) {
  b <- as.vector(spat_extent)  # named xmin/xmax/ymin/ymax, terra's own order
  c(as.numeric(b["xmin"]), as.numeric(b["ymin"]), as.numeric(b["xmax"]), as.numeric(b["ymax"]))
}
wgs84_bounds <- tryCatch({
  poly_wgs84 <- project(as.polygons(ext(r), crs = crs(r)), "EPSG:4326")
  to_minx_miny_maxx_maxy(ext(poly_wgs84))
}, error = function(e) to_minx_miny_maxx_maxy(ext(r)))

con <- rawConnection(raw(0), "wb")
writeBin(as.numeric(filled), con, size = 4, endian = "little")
raw_bytes <- rawConnectionValue(con)
close(con)
filled_b64 <- jsonlite::base64_enc(raw_bytes)

list(
  summary = list(
    targetBand = jsonlite::unbox(target_i),
    covariateBand = if (has_covariate) jsonlite::unbox(covariate_i) else NULL,
    variogramModel = jsonlite::unbox(variogramModel),
    nmax = jsonlite::unbox(as.numeric(nmax)),
    pixelsFilled = jsonlite::unbox(n_filled),
    pixelsStillEmpty = jsonlite::unbox(n_still_na),
    crossValidationRmse = if (is.na(rmse)) NULL else jsonlite::unbox(round(rmse, 4)),
    nugget = jsonlite::unbox(round(nugget_val, 4)),
    partialSill = jsonlite::unbox(round(partial_sill_val, 4)),
    range = jsonlite::unbox(round(range_val, 3)),
    sampleMean = jsonlite::unbox(round(sample_mean, 4)),
    sampleVariance = jsonlite::unbox(round(sample_variance, 4)),
    # Only surfaced when the Cressie-weighted fit (fit.method=7,
    # gstat's own default -- tried first, fits noticeably better) had
    # to fall back to the cruder N-only weighting -- the expected path
    # stays silent, same "only mention the exceptional state" pattern
    # "Still empty" below already uses.
    fitMethodFallback = if (has_covariate && fit_method_used == 1) jsonlite::unbox(TRUE) else NULL
  ),
  raster = list(
    width = jsonlite::unbox(ncol(r)),
    height = jsonlite::unbox(nrow(r)),
    data = jsonlite::unbox(filled_b64),
    wgs84Bounds = round(wgs84_bounds, 6),
    min = jsonlite::unbox(round(min(valid_filled), 4)),
    max = jsonlite::unbox(round(max(valid_filled), 4))
  ),
  variogram = variogram_out
)
```

```{.webgeods-r #raster-gap-filler-export-r .tool-cell}
#| inject: [targetBand, covariateBand, variogramModel, nmax]
#| package: sf, sp, gstat, terra, jsonlite
# Recomputes the same pipeline (cheap relative to re-reading the
# source file) and writes the filled target band as an actual GeoTIFF
# via terra::writeRaster() -- same structure as
# kriging-interpolator-export-r.
library(sf)
library(sp)
library(gstat)
library(terra)

target_i <- as.integer(targetBand)
covariate_i <- if (identical(covariateBand, "None")) NA_integer_ else as.integer(covariateBand)

r <- rast("/uploaded.tif")
cell_xy <- crds(r, na.rm = FALSE)
target_vals <- as.numeric(values(r[[target_i]]))
df <- data.frame(x = cell_xy[, 1], y = cell_xy[, 2], target = target_vals)

has_covariate <- !is.na(covariate_i)
if (has_covariate) df$covariate <- as.numeric(values(r[[covariate_i]]))

if (!has_covariate) {

  fit_df <- df[!is.na(df$target), ]
  pred_df <- df[is.na(df$target), ]
  fit_pts <- fit_df
  coordinates(fit_pts) <- ~x + y
  v_emp <- variogram(target ~ 1, fit_pts)
  v_model <- fit.variogram(v_emp, vgm(psill = var(fit_df$target), model = variogramModel, range = max(v_emp$dist) / 3, nugget = var(fit_df$target) / 4))

  filled <- df$target
  if (nrow(pred_df) > 0) {
    pred_pts <- pred_df
    coordinates(pred_pts) <- ~x + y
    k <- krige(target ~ 1, fit_pts, pred_pts, model = v_model, nmax = as.numeric(nmax), debug.level = 0)
    filled[is.na(df$target)] <- as.numeric(k$var1.pred)
  }

} else {

  data_fit <- df[!is.na(df$target) & !is.na(df$covariate), ]
  data_pred <- df[!is.na(df$covariate), ]
  fit_pts <- data_fit
  coordinates(fit_pts) <- ~x + y
  v_emp <- variogram(target ~ 1, fit_pts)
  init_psill <- var(data_fit$target)
  v_cross <- variogram(gstat(gstat(NULL, id = "target", formula = target ~ 1, data = fit_pts), id = "covariate", formula = covariate ~ 1, data = fit_pts))

  # Same multi-start fit as the preview cell above (see its own comment
  # for why a single init_range = max(dist)/3 guess isn't reliable
  # here) -- the downloaded file should reflect whichever fit the
  # reader actually saw on screen, not a cruder one recomputed only
  # for export.
  sse_against_target <- function(model_df) {
    vl <- variogramLine(model_df, dist_vector = v_emp$dist)
    sum((v_emp$gamma - vl$gamma)^2)
  }
  fit_lmc_candidate <- function(init_range) {
    lmc_model <- vgm(psill = init_psill, model = variogramModel, range = init_range, nugget = init_psill / 4)
    fresh_g <- function() gstat(gstat(NULL, id = "target", formula = target ~ 1, data = fit_pts), id = "covariate", formula = covariate ~ 1, data = fit_pts)
    gf <- tryCatch(fit.lmc(v_cross, fresh_g(), model = lmc_model, fit.method = 7, correct.diagonal = 1.01), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(gf)) gf <- tryCatch(fit.lmc(v_cross, fresh_g(), model = lmc_model, fit.method = 1, correct.diagonal = 1.01), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(gf)) return(NULL)
    list(g_fit = gf, sse = sse_against_target(gf$model[["target"]]))
  }
  candidates <- Filter(Negate(is.null), lapply(max(v_cross$dist) * c(1 / 6, 1 / 3, 2 / 3, 1), fit_lmc_candidate))
  if (length(candidates) == 0) {
    stop(paste0("Could not fit a coregionalization model between these two bands (often too few co-located pixels, or the bands aren't actually correlated)."))
  }
  g_fit <- candidates[[which.min(sapply(candidates, function(c) c$sse))]]$g_fit

  pred_pts <- data_pred
  coordinates(pred_pts) <- ~x + y
  g_pred <- gstat(NULL, id = "target", formula = target ~ 1, data = fit_pts)
  g_pred <- gstat(g_pred, id = "covariate", formula = covariate ~ 1, data = pred_pts)
  g_pred$model <- g_fit$model
  k <- predict(g_pred, newdata = pred_pts, nmax = as.numeric(nmax), debug.level = 0)

  filled <- df$target
  pred_index <- which(!is.na(df$covariate))
  cokriged <- is.na(df$target[pred_index])
  filled[pred_index[cokriged]] <- as.numeric(k$target.pred[cokriged])

}

filled_band <- rast(matrix(filled, nrow = nrow(r), ncol = ncol(r), byrow = TRUE), extent = ext(r), crs = crs(r))
names(filled_band) <- names(r)[target_i]

out_path <- "/tmp/raster-gap-filler.tif"
writeRaster(filled_band, out_path, overwrite = TRUE, filetype = "GTiff")
raw_bytes <- readBin(out_path, what = "raw", n = file.info(out_path)$size)
jsonlite::base64_enc(raw_bytes)
```

*First run loads the R engine — expect 1-3 minutes (R's WebAssembly
build is noticeably slower to start than this site's Python tools).
Instant after that, and again each time you come back to this page.*
